title: Extended Care Health Option (ECHO) Eligibility Continuation Reference
content:
An Extended Care Health Option (ECHO) registration continues while DEERS and the case manager show the beneficiary eligible. The continuation terms are the same in all ten tiers, from Extended Care Health Option, Sponsor E-1 to E-5 through Extended Care Health Option, Sponsor O-9 and O-10.

| Event | Continuation term (every tier) |
|---|---|
| Loss of eligibility | the registration ends at the end of the month DEERS shows the loss of active duty family member status, or the case manager ends the qualifying condition |
| Sponsor dies on active duty | the beneficiary is eligible for the transitional survivor period |
| Sponsor retires | ECHO continues for 0 months after the sponsor retires: it ends at retirement |

## Reading the reference

- **End of the month.** Where DEERS shows that a beneficiary has lost active duty family member status, the registration runs to the end of that month rather than ending on the day of the DEERS change.
- **Retirement.** No continuation month follows the sponsor's retirement; 0 months means ECHO ends at retirement.
- **Death on active duty.** The beneficiary of a sponsor who dies on active duty remains eligible for the transitional survivor period.

*Hypothetical illustration, for illustration only:* DEERS shows, partway through a month, that a beneficiary is no longer an active duty family member; the registration ends at the end of that same month.
